content: Break down the argument by first extracting all explicit premises and the conclusion. Then, map these elements into a formal logical structure, explicitly representing any negations and quantifiers. Check for deductive validity by verifying whether the conclusion is an unavoidable consequence of the premises under all interpretations—focusing especially on how negations and quantifiers interact. If any scenario exists where the premises are true but the conclusion is false, classify the argument as invalid; otherwise, classify it as valid.
